narrative:
On August 4, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 39.8%, with 1,013 out of 2,546 scheduled cases taken up across 38 judges. This represents a decrease from August 3, when the court achieved a 44.5% hearing rate with 1,103 out of 2,478 scheduled cases heard.

Judicial performance highlights revealed notable variations across court halls. Judge Vijaykumar A. Patil in Court Hall 32 achieved one of the highest completion rates, hearing 43 of 56 scheduled cases (76.8%). Judge Shivashankar Amarannavar in Court Hall 20 cleared 59 of 89 cases (66.3%) on his main list while fully completing a secondary list of 11 cases (100%). Judge S Vishwajith Shetty in Court Hall 19 managed the heaviest individual load, hearing 101 out of 275 cases (36.7%). In contrast, Court Hall 6 under Judge B M Shyam Prasad saw minimal movement, hearing 1 of 214 cases on its primary roster.

Stage-wise conversion was led by Admission matters, where 243 of 498 scheduled cases were heard (48.8%). Orders comprised the largest stage overall, with 370 of 961 cases heard (38.5%), reflecting a decline from yesterday's 45.6% conversion rate. Preliminary Hearings achieved a 42.8% rate (134 of 313), while Final Hearing conversion rose from 16.5% yesterday to 22.8% today (122 of 535).

Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest portion of the case-type docket with 1,188 scheduled cases, though only 365 were heard (30.7%), down from 44.8% on August 3. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) maintained steady conversion, with 215 of 432 cases heard (49.8%) compared to 46.6% yesterday. Stronger clearance efficiency was observed in Writ Appeals (59.6%) and Regular Second Appeals (58.6%).
